requirement_table.text: ID register at 0x000 reads 0x20960001.
BUILD register at 0x004 reads the USR_ACCESSE2 word.
SCRATCH at 0x008 reads back the written 32-bit value.
SCRATCH resets to 0.
Unmapped addresses read 0.
Writes to unmapped addresses change no register.
h_rdata shows the addressed register within 2 clk cycles of h_re.
h_rdata holds its value until the next h_re.
SEL resets to 0 (clock A).
ACTIVE_SEL equals the last SEL value written once SWITCHING returns to 0.
SWITCHING is 1 from a change of SEL until ACTIVE_SEL equals SEL.
The clock mux is a BUFGCTRL primitive that produces no clock pulse shorter than the shorter source period.
B_DIV reads a value from 1 to 8 equal to the divide applied to the GT reference clock.
MUX_ERRS stays 0 across 1,000 random switches.
MUX_ERRS increments when the binary counter and the Gray twin disagree.
MUX_ERRS increments when the count is not exactly one more than the previous count.
SWITCH_COUNT equals the number of real changes of SEL carried out.
A write of the current SEL value does not change SWITCH_COUNT.
A write to SNAPSHOT latches the low 32 bits of the muxed counter into MUX_COUNT.
GATE_LEN resets to 25,000,000.
Writing START=1 starts a gate of GATE_LEN clk cycles.
START reads 0 on the clock after it is written as 1.
BUSY is 1 for the whole gate.
DONE is 1 after the gate ends.
FREQ_COUNT equals the muxed-clock rising edges in the gate, within 1 count.
sfp_tx_disable is 1 at all times.
The design uses no GT transceiver channel.
Timing closes on all clocks with worst setup slack of 0 ns or more, with clk_mux paths to clk constrained as asynchronous.
jtag_bus.sv is instantiated unchanged.
